subtype: Approach: asking for a job in the first message [Pitfall]
passage: Ishita, let old Kavitha tell you about the worst message I ever sent. I was twenty. I found a director at a big firm on a professional site, and my whole message was: "Hello sir, I am a final-year student looking for a job. Please refer me." Nothing else. No name of my college, no reason why him, no question. I waited two weeks and heard nothing, and I felt insulted. Later, when I was on the other side and receiving such messages, I understood. I did not know who this person was and could not tell if the student was any good. A referral is a favour to someone you trust. I had sent him a request with no relationship behind it.

qa.q: How old was Kavitha when the message was sent?
What was Kavitha feeling after two weeks without a reply?
qa.a: Kavitha felt insulted and ignored, before later understanding why the message had no answer.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Kavitha have used, and why?
qa.a: Kavitha could have written a short note that said who Kavitha was and asked one question about the director's work, because trust must start before a favour like a referral.

qa.q: How would the director have seen that message?
qa.a: The director would see a stranger with no name of a college, no reason for choosing them and no question, so there was nothing to trust or answer.

grounding: Shows asking a stranger for a referral in the very first message and receiving no answer for lack of any relationship.
